Owner of each G0 mesh node:

Equal node counts are not equal work
Each grid node feeds its nearest G0 node. 
The 1° grid has 360 nodes in every row, so toward the poles they crowd together; the mesh stays evenly spaced.
Real 1° graph: 
median 4 grid nodes per G0 in the tropics, 11 poleward of 60°, up to 360 at the North Pole. Coastlines make no difference.
Schematic, not to scale.

Weighting balances the grid across GPUs
Fix: 
weight each G0 node by its grid nodes when partitioning (METIS vertex weights, Mt-KaHyPar node weights, weighted median in RCB)

METIS, 4 GPUs
Unweighted: 
GPU 3 gets 14,140 grid nodes, 34% above the mean. It holds most of the polar ocean.
Weighted: 
every GPU within 1.6% of the mean
Cost: 
G0 and G1 counts become up to 8% uneven
Measured step time
2 GPUs: weighted 2–4% faster (CIs separate)
4 GPUs: no significant difference
Dashed line: mean per GPU. Step times: METIS and Mt-KaHyPar, 3 launches each (jobs 5497/5498).

PhysicsNeMo: exact distributed message passing

What it is
NVIDIA's open-source PyTorch framework for physics-ML
Ships graph models (MeshGraphNet, GraphCast) and their multi-GPU graph support

Why we use it
Exact full-graph training: same result as one GPU
Accepts any node → GPU map, so our partitioners plug in
PyG / DGL distributed sample neighbours, which changes the algorithm

What DistributedGraph does
Builds each GPU's local graph from the owner map
Halo fetch: indexed all-to-all of remote sender features (NCCL)
Backward: reverse all-to-all with summation
How GraphEFM is integrated (no change to the original model code)

1. One DistributedGraph per relation
g2m, m2m per level, up/down, m2g

2. Slice static features
node and edge features to the GPU's part

3. Wrap every layer
halo fetch → original layer on local edges

4. Sync
global-order noise; all-reduce loss and gradients
def forward(self, send, receive, edge):   # LocalLayer wrapping Njord's original layer
    send = relation.graph.get_src_node_features_in_local_graph(send)   # halo exchange
    return self.net(send, receive, edge)                              # original layer, original weights
PhysicsNeMo

Speedup with 95% confidence intervals
4 GPUs vs 1 GPU: 
H64 2.42× [2.38, 2.50] · H128 3.42× [3.42, 3.43]     
2 → 4 GPUs: 
H64 1.35× · H128 1.88× · H256 1.93×
Training step, Mt-KaHyPar, checkpointing on, batches pre-loaded. Ratio of medians; bootstrap CI over launches and 4-step blocks. H64: 3 launches; H128/H256: 1 launch.

Gradient checkpointing on vs off
Checkpointing trades memory for time: 
activations are recomputed in the backward pass. Off: 2 GPUs 732 → 484 ms (1.51×), 4 GPUs 541 → 320 ms (1.69×)
Off needs 3.6× more memory per GPU, 
so it only fits once the graph is split: 4 GPUs without recompute are 4.09× faster than 1 GPU with it
H64, Mt-KaHyPar, batches pre-loaded. Speedup labels vs 1 GPU with checkpointing on. Off cases: 1 launch each. 1 GPU off did not fit in an earlier run, so it was not benchmarked.
